title: Harmonized U.S. Fetal Death Microdata, 1982-2024
description:
A modern, researcher-ready release of harmonized U.S. fetal death microdata for cross-year stillbirth research. Spans 43 years (1982-2024) of NCHS public-use fetal death files reconciled into a single Parquet file with one stable schema, crossing three Standard Report of Fetal Death revisions (1978, 1989, 2003).

Scope. 2,427,233 total records across 43 years (V3b era 1982-1988: 421,125 rows, 1978-revision; V2 era 1989-2002: 762,538 rows, 1989-revision; V2.1 transition 2003-2004: 107,782 rows; V1 era 2005-2024: 1,135,788 rows, 2003-revision transition; +39,574 records for 2023 and +35,648 for 2024). 73 harmonized variables in the base file plus 16 derived analytic variables (89 columns total) in the derived file. ~2.03 million records form the standard NVSR-comparable subset (tabulation_flag == 2 AND residence_status != 4).

Cross-era value-level normalizations. 5 V2 normalizations (B1 fetal_sex, B2 delivery_method_recode, B3 maternal_race_bridged, B4 paternal_age_recode11, B6 delivery_place_recode) extended for V3a (1989-1991, +2 race codes) and V3b (1982-1988, full 1-digit MRACE recode 0-9 mirroring V2's 2-digit logic). B7 TABFLG correction for 2003-2004 transition years per the NCHS errata fetaldeath0304problems.pdf. 3 within_era columns (B5 breech_unrevised, delivery_place_unrevised, maternal_race_bridged_detail) where the underlying concepts/categories are fundamentally incompatible across eras and cross-era groupby is unsafe.

Validation. 90 checks against published NCHS/NVSR statistics (55 V1 + 23 V2/V3 counts + 10 V2/V2.1 rates + 2 latest-year refresh control-count cells): 90 byte-exact matches. All per-year fetal death counts (43 of 43 years) match the published figures exactly. The 6 previously-documented V1 detail-cell tabulation differences (gestational-age proportional redistribution + 43-state cause-of-death reporting area) are unchanged by V2.4 latest-year refresh.

Companion product. For demographic-stratified live-birth denominators (race-, age-, or ethnicity-specific) needed to compute fetal mortality rates, see the U.S. Natality Harmonization Project (Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19363074).
